implementation_notes: Ktor supplies the dispatcher as a routing DSL: routing { get("/orders/{id}") { ... } } matches the request, the handler body is the worker that reads call.parameters and asks an injected service for data, and call.respond(FreeMarkerContent("orders/show.ftl", mapOf("order" to order))) - or JteContent with typed template parameters - both selects and renders the view; the template plugin and its helpers are the view-helper slot and install(StatusPages) centralises error views. What replaces the classic structure is the plugin pipeline plus the template engine; an explicit command hierarchy is justified when requests must be dispatched to several typed actions, and Spring MVC in Kotlin uses @Controller/@GetMapping exactly as Java does.
pitfalls: The template model is a Map<String, Any>: ${order} and the map key agree only at render time, so a typo renders an empty value - JTE's @param declarations restore compile-time checking.
Template engines are separate artifacts (ktor-server-freemarker, ktor-server-jte) installed on the application module; a missing install fails at startup rather than per request.
call.parameters returns null for an unmatched segment, so the common !! idiom turns a bad URL into a 500 unless StatusPages or a null check maps it.
